Aston Villa responded by dominating possession, orchestrating several attacking phases led by John McGinn and Matty Cash , though their initial corner routines failed to find a clinical finish in a crowded penalty area. The drama intensified as the first half drew to a close. In the 40th minute, Ollie Watkins thought he had leveled the score for the visitors, but a lengthy VAR review resulted in the goal being chalked off for offside. The disappointment was short-lived, however, as Aston Villa found their equalizer in the 42nd minute. In the 56th minute, a long ball from goalkeeper Emiliano Martinez remarkably turned into an assist for Ollie Watkins , who finished composedly with his right foot to put the Villans ahead. Burnley ’s response was almost instantaneous. Just two minutes later, Zian Flemming capitalized on an assist from Hannibal Mejbri to restore parity with a well-placed effort, sending the home support into raptures. As the clock ticked down, both managers turned to their benches, with Leon Bailey and James Ward-Prowse among those introduced to break the deadlock. Aston Villa pushed hard for a winner, maintaining 66% possession and launching late attempts through Emiliano Buendia and Douglas Luiz . However, Burnley goalkeeper Max Weiss produced two vital saves in stoppage time to deny the visitors, ensuring that a thrilling encounter ended with the spoils shared at Turf Moor .

matches.title: Nottingham Forest vs Aston Villa
matches.description: Watch Nottingham Forest vs Aston Villa highlights and goals from UEFA Europa League on ReFooty: Football Highlights Hub. Match played on April 30, 2026. The UEFA Europa League spotlight fell on a high-stakes all-English affair on April 30, 2026 , as two historic clubs looked to assert their dominance on the European stage. Under the lights and in front of a passionate crowd of 29,790, the match promised a tactical chess match where the smallest error could define the outcome. A Tense Tactical Battle From the opening whistle, both Nottingham Forest and Aston Villa displayed a cautious approach, prioritizing defensive solidity over reckless abandon. The first half was characterized by a series of set-piece opportunities that failed to test either goalkeeper. Youri Tielemans was active for the visitors, delivering several corners from both flanks, but the Forest backline, marshaled effectively, cleared its lines with ease. Omari Hutchinson was equally busy for the hosts, swinging in deliveries that ultimately found no takers in a crowded penalty area. Opportunities from open play were scarce. Chris Wood thought he might have found a gap in the 17th minute, but the linesman’s flag quickly quelled the excitement. As the halftime interval approached, Nicolas Dominguez also found himself caught in the offside trap, reflecting a period of play where timing and precision were just slightly out of reach for both sides. Despite Aston Villa shading the possession at 51%, the first half ended without a breakthrough, leaving the tactical puzzle for the managers to solve in the dressing room. VAR Intervention and the Breakthrough The second half continued in a similar vein until a moment of controversy ignited the contest in the 68th minute. The referee initially allowed play to continue during a Nottingham Forest attack, but a signal from the VAR room brought the match to a standstill. Upon reviewing the footage on the pitchside monitor, it was determined that Lucas Digne had handled the ball inside the area. Despite heavy protests from the Villa defender, the official pointed to the spot. Chris Wood stepped up to take the responsibility in the 71st minute. The veteran striker kept his composure under immense pressure, striking the ball with his right foot. While Emiliano Martinez guessed correctly and came agonizingly close to a spectacular save, the power was enough to carry the ball into the net. The goal sent the home support into raptures and forced Unai Emery to rethink his strategy for the final twenty minutes. Holding Firm Against the Villa Surge Facing a deficit, Aston Villa looked to their bench for inspiration, introducing Jadon Sancho , Ian Maatsen , and Douglas Luiz in a triple tactical substitution. The pressure from the visitors intensified, and the game became increasingly physical. Youri Tielemans saw his name go into the referee's book following a rough challenge as frustrations began to boil over. Forest remained dangerous on the break, however, and Neco Williams nearly doubled the lead with a header in the 89th minute, only to be denied by a comfortable save from Emiliano Martinez . As the match entered six minutes of stoppage time, Aston Villa threw everything forward. Jadon Sancho carved out a late chance with a powerful drive from outside the box, but Stefan Ortega stood tall to claim the ball and preserve the clean sheet. Morato and Zach Abbott provided crucial clearances in the dying seconds to repel a flurry of crosses from Tielemans . When the final whistle blew, Nottingham Forest had secured a vital victory, built on defensive resilience and a clinical moment from the penalty spot.

The match featured a series of dramatic turns as both sides fought for dominance under the bright lights of the stadium. Semenyo Strikes Early for City On May 24, 2026 , Manchester City welcomed Aston Villa in a match that initially seemed to follow the champions' script. In front of a crowd of 60,332, the home side broke the deadlock in the 23rd minute. Following a corner sequence, Antoine Semenyo connected with a brilliant right-footed volley that flew into the back of the net. City remained largely in control for the remainder of the first half, heading into the break with a 1-0 lead and looking comfortable despite Villa’s organized defensive shape. Watkins Turns the Tide The complexion of the game changed almost immediately after the restart. In the 47th minute, a costly defensive blunder by John Stones gifted Ollie Watkins an open goal, and the striker made no mistake, tapping the ball home with his left foot. The goal was confirmed after a VAR review, signaling the start of a Villa resurgence. The visitors struck again in the 61st minute; Lamare Bogarde played a key pass to Ross Barkley , who set up Ollie Watkins for a clinical finish. Suddenly, the scoreline was flipped, and the visitors held a 2-1 lead. Late VAR Heartbreak at the Etihad As the clock ticked down, Manchester City threw everything at the opposition. Leon Bailey nearly ended the contest in the 76th minute, but his effort struck the post. The drama reached its peak in stoppage time when Phil Foden thought he had rescued a point for the hosts. However, after a lengthy VAR check in the 90+2nd minute, the goal was disallowed for offside. Despite a flurry of late chances and a blocked shot from Mateo Kovacic , Aston Villa held firm to secure a massive comeback victory on the road.

The visitors weren't finished, however, and struck again deep into first-half stoppage time. In the 45+3 minute, Emiliano Buendia turned from provider to scorer, unleashing a powerful left-footed strike from outside the box that left the keeper helpless and doubled the lead. In the 58th minute, Morgan Rogers capitalized on another Buendia assist to slot home the third goal with his right foot. Down 0-3, the German side attempted to refresh their lineup with tactical substitutions, bringing on the likes of Lucas Hoeler and Max Rosenfelder , but they struggled to break through a disciplined Villa backline, frequently being caught in the offside trap. Managers utilized their benches, with Jadon Sancho and Amadou Onana entering the field to see out the result. Villa Park played host to a high-stakes Premier League clash as Aston Villa and Liverpool met in a match full of tactical intrigue. The atmosphere was electric on May 15, 2026 , as both sides looked to assert their dominance in a fixture known for its history and intensity. Breakthrough at Villa Park The match began as a cagey affair, with Liverpool attempting to control possession while Aston Villa looked for openings on the break. Cody Gakpo found himself ruled offside on multiple occasions, frustrating the visitors' early efforts. The deadlock was finally broken in the 42nd minute when Morgan Rogers capitalized on a clever short corner routine. Lucas Digne provided the delivery, and Rogers finished clinically with his right foot to give the home side the lead heading into the break. Rapid Exchanges and VAR Drama The second half saw an immediate shift in momentum. Liverpool responded in the 52nd minute through Virgil van Dijk , who rose highest to head home a Dominik Szoboszlai cross. The goal was subject to a VAR review but was eventually given, bringing the scores level. However, the parity was short-lived. In the 57th minute, a lapse in concentration from Szoboszlai allowed Aston Villa to regain the lead, as Ollie Watkins found the net with a composed right-footed finish following an assist from Morgan Rogers . Watkins Takes Charge As the game entered its final quarter, Aston Villa tightened their grip. In the 73rd minute, Ollie Watkins struck again, surviving another VAR check to make it 3-1. Liverpool introduced Mohamed Salah in an attempt to salvage the game, but the hosts remained clinical. In the 89th minute, John McGinn effectively ended the contest, beating the keeper from outside the box with a powerful left-footed strike after being set up by Watkins . There was still time for late drama in stoppage time as Virgil van Dijk headed in his second goal of the night from another Szoboszlai corner, but it proved to be a mere consolation. In front of an attendance of 43,033, the referee blew the final whistle to confirm a deserved victory for the Villans , with Ollie Watkins standing out as a key performer in the high-scoring victory.
